findings.title: R-2 fix still lets grouped broad regexes bypass confirmation
findings.body: `topLevelAlternatives` ignores `|` inside groups. Direct evaluation of `^(https://ads\.example\.net/|https://.*\.com/)` returns `narrow`, although its second branch matches every HTTPS `.com` URL and avoids both `.invalid` probes. RuleForm only requests confirmation for `wide`, so this destructive Block is enabled on the first save. The added tests cover top-level alternatives, allowing all focused tests to pass against the wrong risk surface.
findings.recommendation: Return `narrow` only when every alternative at every nesting level is proven host-bound; otherwise default to `wide`. Add the grouped counterexample to the pure-function table and an end-to-end first-save confirmation test.

findings.title: R-3 migration fix can overwrite a newer user command
findings.body: `commitMigration` retains a migrated v1 snapshot and later persists it outside the command executor’s FIFO queue. The command listener is already active before startup migration begins (`background-bootstrap.ts:262-295`), so a command can persist edited v2 state before the stale migration write finishes. `persistState` only checks readability, not snapshot identity, and therefore accepts the stale overwrite. A controlled execution saved `Changed` and then finished with `Legacy`. Existing tests exercise only sequential commits.
findings.recommendation: Put migration and commands behind the same background write barrier or queue. Add a deferred-storage regression test where a command persists v2 while migration is pending and assert that the command’s state remains authoritative.

findings.title: Snapshot deletion can silently erase a concurrent automatic backup
findings.body: `deleteBackupSnapshot` reads and later replaces the entire manifest without serialization against `performBackup`, which independently writes that manifest from the automatic-backup path. If backup commits between deletion’s read and manifest write, deletion overwrites the new entry; verification checks only that the deleted ID is absent and returns success. A controlled interleaving produced `{ok:true}`, an empty manifest, and the new backup’s orphaned chunk. Smoke N43 explicitly makes late automatic backup take the skip path (`scripts/smoke.mjs:4273-4276`), so committed evidence avoids this production race.
findings.recommendation: Route deletion and automatic backup through one background writer per target, then add a deterministic test interleaving their manifest commits. For sync updates, preserve unrelated entries through revision/conflict-aware retry.
